findings.reason: §3 must be reduced to the genuinely missing parts (the all-guards `--dry-run`, the reason-taking-flag swallow refusal) and expressed as an extension of `promotion_records.py`/`reuse reports.py`, or it will land a parallel receipt validator beside a working one.
findings.text: §3's deliverable ("complete reads the gate receipt the run's manifest carries: the command, the exit status, the log path and the commits. It validates the receipt. The log must be a file under the run directory whose last `EXIT=<n>` line equals the stated status. Each commit must resolve…") is already in the tree, so §3 as written re-implements working code: `promotion_records.py:231`'s docstring reads "Fill a passing promotion's gate flags from the worker's own manifest… the manifest states the gate command in `tests`, the log path in `test_logs`, its exit status on the log's own `EXIT=` line, and the commits in `commits`. Each is taken only where the operator's flag left the value absent, so an explicit `--gate-command` or `--commit` always wins" — which is §3 bullets 1 and 2 verbatim in behaviour; `reports.py:287` `parse_manifest` is the manifest reader §3 would need; `reports.py:1097` `_EXIT_RECORD`/`reports.py:1101` `_terminal_exit_status` read only an end-of-log `EXIT=<n>` and `reports.py:1304` already refuses a log "ends with no `EXIT=<n>` line" — §3's stated log validation and its `EXIT=1` beside a stated `0` negative control; and `promotion_scope.py:265` `_resolve_commits` already refuses a commit that "does not resolve to a commit object in the run repository", which is §3's second negative control. The plan measures its premise at `d8ff471c9` and does not restate it at a revision where this machinery is absent.

findings.reason: the author must add `promotion_records.py`, `promotion_scope.py`, `reports.py`, `claims.py`, `gc.py`, `mcp.py` and `mcp_views.py` to the scopes that touch their behaviour, drop the nonexistent `promotion_receipt.py`, and name the owner each new file extends instead of forking it.
findings.text: each section re-specifies behaviour owned by a file its write paths omit, and one write path names a module that does not exist: §3's write paths list `reckon/crew/promotion_receipt.py`, which `ls` reports absent on this revision, while omitting `promotion_records.py:231` (the receipt filler) and `promotion_scope.py:265`/`reports.py:1097` (commit resolution and the `EXIT=` reader) that exist and own exactly that work; §4's write paths list `reckon/crew/merge.py` but add a new `reckon/crew/landing.py`, while `merge.py:309` `land_merge` already builds the merge and pushes it (`_push_and_confirm`, with the port-443 fallback §4 step 3 asks for) and `promotion_release.py:476` `_release_after_promotion` already releases the worktree through `gc`'s removal; §7 names `complete --accept-path` "writes the same fence record through it" but its write paths omit `reckon/crew/claims.py:90` `narrow_claim`/`reckon/crew/claims.py:128` `release_claim`, the owner of the fence/claim record, and `reckon/crew/gc.py:262` `garbage_collect`, which §4 step 4 defers to; §6 says `crew view` serves "through the same function" the MCP `crew` tool serves, but no such function exists — `reckon/mcp.py:1621` `_crew` is a ~200-line inline view dispatch, and `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:221` `crew_list` hand-builds its own ~25-field row set rather than calling it — and §6's write paths omit `reckon/mcp.py` and `reckon/mcp_views.py`, where that function must be extracted for the parity its own done-when asserts.

findings.reason: the plan should either place the sequence in `merge.py` (where the merge and push already live) or justify a separate module; as written it adds a path where an extension would do.
findings.text: `crew complete --land` (the plan's §4 deliverable) introduces a new module `reckon/crew/landing.py` that sequences four steps already held by `merge.py:309`, `promotion_release.py:476` and `gc.py:262`, and the section does not say why those existing mechanisms cannot carry the sequence — the honest change looks like a `land` function beside `land_merge` in `reckon/crew/merge.py`, or a promotion-time delay of the existing release, not a fourth module over the same three calls.

findings.reason: §1 already accounts for the retained CLI surface and the fold is net-reducing (65 visible leaves), so §5's growth is stated rather than unowned.
findings.text: §5 adds eight actions (`complete`, `land`, `dispose`, `ack`, `answer`, `widen`, `stop`, `discard`) to the `crew` MCP tool without naming, in §5's own text, what it retires or merges on the tool side, against this week's mcp_views 34 — though §1 does state that the CLI remains the worker and hook transport, which is the reason nothing CLI-side can be withdrawn by this section.

response_events.reason: §1 accounts for the retained CLI surface: the CLI stays the worker and hook transport, and the fold is net-reducing to about 65 visible leaves, as the finding itself records.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §2's tombstone registry (`reckon/crew/tombstones.py`) is one table plus one registration path hiding per-row successor resolution, and §6's `crew view` hides the view dispatch behind one verb; both are interfaces smaller than the behaviour behind them.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the re-specified mechanisms census below names five existing owners that the plan's write scopes omit.

rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan re-specifies the gate-receipt and commit-resolution machinery that `reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:231`, `reckon/crew/reports.py:287` and `reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:265` already implement, and cites none of them.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4 adds `reckon/crew/landing.py` beside `reckon/crew/merge.py:309` (which already merges *and* pushes) and `reckon/crew/promotion_release.py:476` (which already releases after promotion), without saying why those two cannot be extended.
